label: R0.4-RC2 Cloudflare Functions type-error inventory
pii_policy: This inventory carries no raw user content, no Telegram payloads, no credentials and no PII. Only file paths, symbol names, TypeScript codes and dispositions.

findings.description: The request body's `status` was asserted to `AiDraftStatus` before validation, so the closed settable list rejected the widened argument.
findings.runtime_risk_note: The runtime guard already rejected non-members; the assertion only hid that the parsed value was untrusted.
findings.security_relevance_note: This is the gate that stops a reviewer from writing the terminal `imported` status without going through the import endpoint.
findings.proposed_fix: Read the body as `unknown`, keep a `SETTABLE_STATUSES` const tuple, and parse with a cast-free closed-list guard that fails closed on any non-member.
findings.behavioral_test: draft status: valid settable status is accepted and persisted; unknown status values fail closed with 400 and no write; missing status is rejected; "imported" cannot be set here — no auto-publish path

findings.description: `withErrorHandler` was called without its environment type argument, so `E` fell back to `unknown` and `EventContext` collapsed `env` to the ambient `{ ASSETS }` binding. Every project binding the aggregator reads then looked undeclared.
findings.runtime_risk_note: Purely a lost type argument. The reads themselves were always correct at runtime.
findings.security_relevance_note: The untyped environment hid which secrets the endpoint touches, weakening review of the `system` disclosure block.
findings.proposed_fix: Annotate the export as `PagesFunction<Env>` and pass `withErrorHandler<Env>`, matching the idiom every other admin endpoint already uses.
findings.behavioral_test: cockpit: reads real environment bindings into the system section; requires admin authentication

findings.description: Nullable and unknown-shaped D1 aggregate rows were consumed through the same untyped environment. Reviewed alongside F-02 and covered by dedicated null/unknown-row tests.
findings.runtime_risk_note: The existing `?? 0` / `?? null` coalescing and the try/catch around the schedule setting already handled null and malformed rows; the behaviour is now pinned by tests instead of only by inspection.
findings.security_relevance_note: The summaries must stay bounded counts with no PII; the new tests assert that.
findings.proposed_fix: No source change required beyond F-02; add behavioural tests that drive null titles, an unrecognised status value and a malformed settings row.
findings.behavioral_test: cockpit: null and unrecognised D1 values are handled without failing the section; a failing upstream degrades one section instead of the response; the analytics payload carries no PII and no credential material

findings.description: `fingerprint.entity` was read three times, but `IntentFingerprint` exposes the entity axis as `primary_entity` and has never had an `entity` field. The expression always evaluated to `undefined`, so `body.cluster || fingerprint.entity || null` has only ever produced `body.cluster || null`.
findings.runtime_risk_note: Dead read. Adopting `primary_entity` instead would START writing the heuristic bucket (frequently the literal 'none') into the plan item, the reservation row and the generator brief — a product change, not a type fix.
findings.security_relevance_note: `cluster_key` is not part of the reservation uniqueness index, so idempotency is unaffected either way.
findings.proposed_fix: Hoist a single `clusterKey = body.cluster || null` with the rationale documented in place, and remove the dead read. Behaviour is preserved byte-for-byte.
findings.behavioral_test: quick launch: cluster_key comes from the request only — the fingerprint bucket never leaks in; an explicit cluster from the request is stored verbatim
findings.follow_up_for_owner: Whether `primary_entity` SHOULD populate cluster_key is an open product question, deliberately not decided in a type-safety sprint.

findings.description: The normaliser cast `Record<string, unknown>[]` to `AiDraftArticle[]`, claiming a validated shape it does not produce. Its own comment admitted the articles were 'typed loosely'.
findings.runtime_risk_note: The cast made an unvalidated payload look validated to every reader of `NormaliseSuccess`. The only consumer, `ingestRawBundle`, accepts `unknown` and re-validates, so no bad data actually reached D1.
findings.security_relevance_note: This is the boundary where provider output enters the AI Draft Inbox. It must stay untrusted until `validateIncomingBundle` runs.
findings.proposed_fix: Introduce `NormalisedArticleCandidate` (canonical key names, collections still `unknown[]`) and `NormalisedDraftBundle`, type `normaliseArticle` with it, replace `.filter(Boolean) as …` with a real type-guard predicate, and drop the cast.
findings.behavioral_test: normaliser: a valid RU+UZ bundle produces both locales with forced safe envelope values; unknown keys are dropped and the schema stays closed; malformed provider responses fail deterministically; the failure reason never reflects raw model output; normaliser output still has to clear the strict validator, which bounds oversized fields

findings.description: `AnalysisProviderResult extends SanitizedAnalysisResult` while redeclaring `errorCode` as a strict superset. An interface member may narrow but never widen the one it inherits.
findings.runtime_risk_note: The handler's abstain branch keys off `insufficient_content`; the broken extension meant the transport codes were not reliably part of the checked union.
findings.security_relevance_note: Analysis error codes are written to analytics. Keeping the list closed is what stops provider prose from leaking into event metadata.
findings.proposed_fix: Split the closed lists into `SanitizeErrorCode`, `AnalysisTransportErrorCode` and their union `AnalysisErrorCode`; extend via `Omit<SanitizedAnalysisResult, 'errorCode'>` so the superset relation is stated instead of violated.
findings.behavioral_test: analysis: transport failures and sanitizer failures live in one closed union; a non-object provider payload is invalid_json; insufficient content abstains; an unsafe verdict is dropped entirely; summary and quotes are bounded

findings.description: `TgItemRow.source_text` is `string | null`, but `generateReply` requires `string`. `getOwnedItem` already rejects rows whose `source_text` was cleared, so the guarantee existed at runtime and was simply absent from the type. Downstream call sites papered over it with four non-null assertions.
findings.boundary_type: D1 row after the ownership + retention gate
findings.runtime_risk_note: The unjustified `!` assertions would have silently produced `undefined` prompts if the gate ever changed. The purge path (voice retention, TTL sweep) is exactly the case that clears the column.
findings.security_relevance_note: This is the content-retention boundary: a purged transcript must never be resumable through a replayed callback.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `TgOwnedItemRow extends TgItemRow { source_text: string }`, narrow inside `getOwnedItem` with a `row is TgOwnedItemRow` predicate, return the narrowed type, take it in `runAnalysis`/`runModifier`, and delete all four non-null assertions.
findings.behavioral_test: telegram: getOwnedItem enforces ownership, retention and the source-text guarantee; a callback replay after the retention purge is stale and never regenerates; a callback for another user's item is refused without disclosing it; unsupported, malformed and incomplete updates are absorbed deterministically; a repeated update_id is claimed once

observed_not_in_scope.observation: The 500 branch reports `(e as Error).message` on the wire. This is an unsafe cast and an unbounded error disclosure, but it produced no typecheck error and changing it would change the response body. Left untouched under scope control; recorded here for a future error-normaliser task.
